system_description.narrative_title: Post-midterm Realignment: Democratic Gains, GOP Turmoil, Trump Pushback
system_description.narrative_summary: The 2026 midterm results produced a Democratic surge that reshaped control of legislatures and federal power, prompting plans for oversight, investigations, and a Democratic policy agenda while provoking sharp GOP infighting and blame-shifting. As an open system, key actors (Democratic leadership, GOP factions, former President Trump and his advisers, the Justice Department, courts, media and markets) exchange flows of political power, legal actions, funding, and narratives; feedback loops (investigations → counter-investigations → legal rulings → public opinion → electoral prospects) and time-bound catalysts (appointments, impeachment moves, court decisions) steer system dynamics. These interactions transmit shocks into policy domains (trade, AI, health regulation) and into international perceptions, producing non-linear risks of escalation, institutional stress, or political realignment.
system_description.scope: U.S. federal political ecosystem in the immediate aftermath of the midterms: composition and leadership of Congress, White House personnel changes and directives, DOJ and federal investigations, oversight/impeachment actions, major federal policy levers (tariffs, appropriations, AI regulation, health/drug oversight), and national media and markets reacting to these shifts.
system_description.super_system: American democratic-political-economic system (the electorate, state governments, national economy, and international economic and geopolitical environment).
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. media and public opinion ecosystem
Judicial and legal system (federal courts, ethics probes)
State and local politics and electoral machinery
evidence_headlines: Democrats Win Victories on a Historic Scale
Trump taps immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as chief of staff
Republican infighting mounts over corruption claims after midterms wipeout
Democrats vow to impeach Trump officials and investigate Republican donors
The Red Wall Falls: Democrats Shatter Decades of GOP Dominance Across the South

variables.name: Distribution of Formal Power
variables.description: Measures the relative allocation of formal policymaking control across national decision-making bodies and offices at a given time.

variables.name: Administrative Policy Influence
variables.description: Measures the effective capacity of the administrative apparatus to initiate, shape, and implement policy outcomes.

variables.name: Interparty Polarization
variables.description: Measures the degree of ideological distance and adversarial posture between primary political groupings.

variables.name: Intraparty Cohesion
variables.description: Measures the internal alignment and cooperative coordination among members of the same political grouping.

variables.name: Oversight and Investigation Intensity
variables.description: Measures the rate and intensity of oversight actions and investigative processes initiated by political actors.

variables.name: Legal Proceedings Pressure
variables.description: Measures the frequency and force of formal legal actions, prosecutions, and counterclaims affecting political actors.

variables.name: Adjudicative Constraint
variables.description: Measures the extent to which adjudicative authority can alter, delay, or block policy implementation and political actions.

variables.name: Public Opinion Alignment
variables.description: Measures the net alignment of public preferences with competing policy positions and political groupings.

variables.name: Media Narrative Salience
variables.description: Measures the prominence and intensity of specific narratives and frames in mass and social media coverage.

variables.name: Campaign and Donor Funding Flow
variables.description: Measures the volume and velocity of monetary and in-kind resources mobilized and transferred for political campaigning and influence.

variables.name: Policy Agenda Momentum
variables.description: Measures the pace at which prioritized policy items advance through proposal, negotiation, and enactment stages.

variables.name: Regulatory Action Rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and magnitude of regulatory issuances, rulemaking activity, and enforcement actions over time.

variables.name: Market Political Sensitivity
variables.description: Measures the responsiveness of financial and economic market indicators to political developments and policy signals.

variables.name: Policy Uncertainty Level
variables.description: Measures the perceived unpredictability of near-term policy choices, legal outcomes, and regulatory directions.

variables.name: Administrative Personnel Turnover
variables.description: Measures the rate at which senior administrative and political appointees and key staff positions are vacated and replaced.

variables.name: Electoral Competitiveness
variables.description: Measures the closeness and volatility of electoral contests and the likelihood of seat changes across electoral cycles.

catalysts.title: Democratic probes of Trump, donors, and corporations
catalysts.description: Incoming Democratic committees pursue wide-ranging investigations of Trump officials, major donors and corporate figures, producing subpoenas, hearings and litigation. This sustained oversight drive will dominate early congressional agenda-setting and press coverage.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Democrats vow to impeach Trump officials and investigate Republican donors'; 'Democrats plan probes of Musk, Miller, corporate America.'

catalysts.title: Lame‑duck rush to advance Trump judicial picks
catalysts.description: Senate Republicans pursue a lame‑duck effort to confirm Trump‑aligned judges before the new Congress, pressuring quick floor action and committee votes. Outcomes will shape judicial balance and litigation outcomes for years.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Senate Republicans kick off lame-duck dash to advance Trump judge picks.'

catalysts.title: Democratic flood of AI bills
catalysts.description: Democratic committee agendas prioritize a large package of AI governance and oversight bills early in the next Congress, driving rulemaking, hearings and possible expedited floor action. This will set regulatory direction for the tech sector.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Democrats planning flood of AI bills when they take control of Congress.'

catalysts.title: Elizabeth Warren assumes Senate banking chair
catalysts.description: When the new Senate convenes, Elizabeth Warren will take the banking committee chair and push aggressive oversight and regulatory initiatives affecting finance and markets. Expect high‑profile hearings and rule proposals.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Elizabeth Warren set to take over the Senate banking committee'; 'Elizabeth Warren’s Power in New Senate Is a Wall Street Nightmare.'

catalysts.title: Hard‑line White House strategy under Stephen Miller
catalysts.description: Trump's elevation of Stephen Miller signals a more combative White House posture — sharper immigration, legal and rhetorical offensives and directed DOJ actions — sustaining partisan conflict with Democrats.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Donald Trump taps immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as chief of staff'; 'Trump orders DOJ to look into Democrats.'

catalysts.title: Post‑election DOJ resignations and turnover
catalysts.description: A post‑election exodus at the Justice Department accelerates, producing vacancies and interim leadership that could slow enforcement, complicate prosecutions, and increase policy uncertainty.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Two top Justice Department officials resign as post-election exodus accelerates'; 'Head of US Justice Department's civil division resigns.'

catalysts.title: Special‑master oversight and litigation in Trump DC golf suit
catalysts.description: A special master was appointed in the ethics lawsuit over Trump's DC golf project, initiating review and potential court actions that will keep legal pressure and media attention on Trump enterprises.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: ''Special master' named for ethics probe in lawsuit over Trump's DC golf project.'

catalysts.title: Republican infighting and party realignment
catalysts.description: Post‑midterm blame games and leadership fights produce prolonged GOP factionalism as potential 2028 contenders jockey, weakening cohesion and altering electoral strategies across states.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Republican infighting mounts after midterms wipeout'; 'Battle to reclaim the Republican Party.'

catalysts.title: Senate advance on infrastructure/permitting bills
catalysts.description: Senate movement on bipartisan bills to speed infrastructure and energy permitting could produce near‑term votes and rule changes affecting projects, tribes and regulatory timelines.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Senate advances Trump-backed bipartisan bill to speed critical infrastructure projects'; 'Senate advances energy permitting bill opposed by some Democrats, tribes.'
